projects.title: idea.quest
projects.pitch: A vault-backed project tracker being redesigned as a cozy potion room with data-driven progress jars.
projects.nextMove: Review the running local context-chat prototype at http://127.0.0.1:4189/. Its first grounded answer passed; decide keep or revise. Public site and 3D Step 3 remain unchanged.

updates.text: User approved a bounded local read-only context-chat spike. The separate site now shows recorded status and sources; an actual Codex prompt correctly reported idea.quest 2/5 and the paused unapproved 3D Step 3. Await user review; no gate or public deployment changed.

User clarified that context and understanding matter more than sharing the exact Claudian session. Proposed a local read-only chat test with explicit vault context; no chat build, remote access, or gate approved.

Paused 3D Step 3 review to explore a Codex chat/status side feature. Feasibility note compares status-only, local chat, and owner-only remote bridge. Public site is unchanged; no new gate or chat route approved.

Built an isolated read-only Three.js feasibility slice. The real registry now yields 2/2/5; a clearly labelled in-memory demo shows 0/2/5. Local browser and automated checks passed; visual approval remains pending.
User chose and approved Route C, a Three.js 3D room, with the existing public ASCII site kept live. Step 3 begins as an isolated small test; no public redesign deployment.
User provisionally approved Step 1's Midnight Workshop goal and three-jar scope. Only the Goal gate advanced; route and build remain pending.
Potion-room redesign drafted for review: one table, an original cat witch, and three data-driven jars. Goal gate remains unapproved; existing project records are preserved.
The ASCII cat now blinks, flicks its tail, and winks on hover; it also appears in the compact layout and respects reduced motion.
Added restrained icon motion, press/hover feedback, and approval-only checkpoint animation; reduced-motion preference disables them.
An owner-private read-only web mirror was deployed. It checks the public vault repo after sync; online edits are not enabled.
A working local prototype was built. No workflow gate is marked approved just because it runs.
